messages:
Maya: heads up — console charts are noticeably slower on the recent canary deploy (09:12). FCP +200ms on heatmap pages :grimacing:
Evan: saw that, reproducing locally. Telemetry shows a CPU spike during hydration and a ~300KB jump in the charting chunk since the last bundle split PR.
Lin: reproduced here too. Timeline shows long parse/compile between 200–450ms on first load. Flamegraph looks like most time in parsing the vendor chunk.
deploy-bot: deploy canary-redwood-console@2026-03-19T09:12:05 completed to canary :white_check_mark:
Evan: bundle analyzer points at react-visuals v3 being pulled in with several adapters — bundle went from ~120KB -> ~420KB for charts chunk. Also noticed KV cache miss rate up for heatmap prefixes (more cold builds).
Priya: we merged the split that colocated intl + chart libs into the same chunk in PR #4321. That could cause the big spike on pages that previously only loaded intl.
Nate: quick hypothesis: increased chunk size delays parse/hydration which blocks interactive paint. Also prefetch heuristics may not trigger for some routes, so we get cold loads.
Maya: suggestions: 1) split chart core out as its own async chunk, 2) add route-hover prefetch for heatmap route, 3) move heavy transforms to a web worker to avoid main-thread stalls.
Lin: small repro command I used:
```
NODE_ENV=development yarn start --canary --profile --open /dash/heatmap
```
Gives consistent 350ms parse time on my M1 and ~450ms on a populated CI runner.
Evan: I'm going to try isolating react-visuals imports and measure parse times. If split is trivial we can patch canary and push to 10% A/B. If nontrivial revert PR #4321.
Priya: I'll run bundle-analyzer (+ source-map-explorer) and post a snapshot in a bit. Also checking if our chunking config accidentally set preferred max chunk size too high.
Nate: temporary mitigation: we can enable streaming hydration for chart routes to get interactivity earlier, but that'll be a bit of engineering.
Maya: agree — prefer small revert if easy. If we patch, do canary -> 10% A/B -> full. If revert, coordinate rollback window.
Evan: assigning to me, will post numbers by EOD. @Priya please include before/after analyzer images. :eyes:
Priya: on it, uploading analyzer shot shortly.
Maya: ping #eng-oncall if you see >3x regression in production. Keeping this thread focused on root cause + quick mitigations. Thanks all. :pray:
